newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH DENY PLANS TO SELL MISSILES TO TURKEY.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH DENY PLANS TO SELL MISSILES TO TURKEY.

text.p: The Netherlands said on Tuesday it had no plans to sell surface-to-air missiles to Turkey and that media reports to that effect were incorrect.
Belgium confirmed on Monday that French company Thomson-CSF was negotiating a possible sale of surplus Belgian Hawk missiles to Turkey.
Media reports had said the talks also covered a possible sale of surplus Dutch Hawk missiles but the Dutch defence and foreign ministries both denied this.
"As far as the Netherlands is concerned we are not going to sell Hawks to Turkey," a defence ministry spokesman said.
The Netherlands had not taken any initiative in this regard, nor had it been approached by Turkey or Thomson-CSF, he said.
A foreign ministry spokesman also said the Netherlands was not considering the sale of missiles to Turkey.
"There is no request to supply missiles to Turkey via Thomson...there is no question of a sale," he said.
On Monday Belgian government spokesmen said Thomson-CSF was discussing the sale to Turkey of Belgian missiles but that the government had not yet decided whether it would approve a sale.

Talk of missile sales to Turkey has coincided with renewed tension between Turkey and Greece over the divided Mediterranean island of Cyprus where the Greek Cypriot government plans to deploy S-300 anti-aircraft missiles bought from Russia.
